audit.evidence: Useful tips for designing a robust database schema. This guide is more of a decision reference (1) for people wanting to design better database schemas for startups (2). ／ - Decision reference: You will probably come across any one of the problems below when designing database schema (e.g. should I use `JSONB`? How do I design `tagging` schema? How do I keep historical records?) and be presented with different options and trade-offs. If two standards are equal (should table name be singular or plural), then it's up to you to pick one and make it a standard and keeping it consistent. Rather than giving you a `it depends` answer, this guide is meant to share the `what-ifs`, that is the decision I made, and the outcome. Yes, the codes are actually being written and used in different applications I wrote. You don't have to agree with the approaches - I used to take some of the more complex approaches (for the sake of _best practice_), but over time I realised that it is unnecessary. Simple is best. ／ - Startups: A lot of startups starts by using ORMs or frameworks that provides a lot of convenience when it comes to dealing with database. If you are thinking _hey, we need to be agile, that's why we are okay introducing some technical debts_ let me tell you something, you can be both fast and produce quality work (not compromising database design). Most of the time, when new features are being introduced, or when new situation aroses (e.g. analytics are not accurate, because we did not store timestamp with timezones in database, using integer id instead of uuid, and people start _hacking_ your system, etc), the application just won't cut it anymore. The last thing I want to live with is a poorly designed database schema. You can switch language and frameworks for your frontend/backend servers, but if you design your database wrongly, you have to live with it. Also, I mentioned `startups` because my knowledge on database design is limited to a user scale of `<5m`. Also, the approach taken by larger companies might vary, and the technology used might differ as they are focusing a lot on performance, reliability and running databases across the world. For this guide, we are talking specifically about `mysql` and `postgres`, and probably just running them in cloud providers like AWS/Google Cloud.

identity.review: 这是 Aplus Framework 生态中的会话管理库，以 PHP 库形式发布在 Packagist，支持通过 composer 安装。从主题标签看其会话存储后端可涉及 cookie、文件、数据库与 memcached 等。README 内容极简，主要链接到主页、用户指南与 API 文档，适用于使用 Aplus 框架的 PHP 开发者。
highlights: 提供会话管理功能，作为 Aplus Framework 的组件库
主题标签显示支持 cookie、database、files、memcached 等会话相关存储途径
通过 composer 发布，附测试与覆盖率信息
use_cases: 在 Aplus Framework 项目中管理用户会话
需要多种会话存储后端（文件、数据库、memcached）的 PHP 应用

classification.eco_why: 它是为框架生态提供的会话库组件，主题标签含 database/memcached 表明可对接数据库存储，属服务生态的工具/组件

audit.evidence: Aplus Framework Session Library ／ packagist

identity.one_liner: 为 ActiveRecord 迁移提供数据库约束 DSL 的 Ruby 库
identity.review: Rein 是一个 Ruby gem，在 ActiveRecord 迁移中添加一系列约束方法（外键、唯一、排除、CHECK 等），使用户无需手写 SQL 即可在数据库层面声明数据完整性规则，且所有 DSL 方法可逆，支持 Rails 可逆迁移。面向使用 Rails/ActiveRecord 并在数据库层实施约束的开发者；从排除约束等特性看主要面向 PostgreSQL。
highlights: 提供外键、唯一、排除、包含、长度、正则、数值性、存在性等约束的声明式 DSL
所有 DSL 方法自动可逆，兼容 Rails 可逆迁移
支持 NOT VALID、延迟检查（deferred）与条件约束等选项
use_cases: 在 Rails 应用中以数据库级约束保障数据完整性
在迁移中使用排除约束防止范围重叠
对已有大表以 NOT VALID 方式并发添加约束
